Calculate Structural Concordance Between Geomorphon and Categorical Maps

Source: R/analysis.R
geomorphon_concordance.Rd

Measures the degree of structural agreement between a geomorphon classification and another categorical map (e.g., soil types, vegetation classes) using Normalized Mutual Information and boundary alignment metrics.

Usage

geomorphon_concordance(
  geo_rast,
  cat_rast,
  method = c("both", "nmi", "boundary"),
  threshold_cells = 2,
  spatial_null = TRUE
)

Arguments

geo_rast

SpatRaster. Geomorphon classification raster (typically output from geomorphons()).

cat_rast

SpatRaster. Categorical comparison raster (e.g., soil map, vegetation map). Must have matching extent and resolution to geo_rast.

method

Character. Which concordance metrics to calculate. One of "nmi" (Normalized Mutual Information only), "boundary" (boundary alignment only), or "both" (all metrics). Default: "both".

threshold_cells

Integer. Buffer distance in cells for boundary concordance calculation, converted to map units with the cell size. Categorical boundary cells within this distance of the nearest geomorphon boundary cell are counted as concordant. Must be a finite, non-negative whole number when method includes boundary metrics. Geographic (longitude/latitude) CRS inputs are rejected with an error when method includes boundary metrics because boundary distances require a planar Cartesian CRS. Default: 2.

spatial_null

Logical. Whether to calculate the spatial-null ensemble. If FALSE, skip it and return NA_real_ null means/deltas and zero shift counts. Default: TRUE.

Value

A list with the following components (depending on method):

nmi

Numeric. Normalized Mutual Information (0-1). Higher values indicate stronger statistical association between classifications. Existing NMI behavior is unchanged. Only included when method includes "nmi".

homogeneity

Numeric. I(geo; cat) / H(cat), measuring how well the geomorphon classes determine the categorical reference. NA_real_ when H(cat) = 0; otherwise zero for a constant geomorphon map against a varying categorical map. Included only for methods "nmi" and "both".

completeness

Numeric. I(geo; cat) / H(geo), measuring how completely the categorical classes capture geomorphon information. NA_real_ when H(geo) = 0; otherwise zero for a constant categorical map against a varying geomorphon map. Included only for methods "nmi" and "both".

edge_offset

Numeric. Mean distance (in map units) from each categorical boundary cell to the nearest geomorphon boundary cell. Lower values indicate better boundary alignment. Only included when method includes "boundary".

edge_concordance

Numeric. Proportion (0-1) of categorical boundary cells within threshold_cells of the nearest geomorphon boundary cell. Higher values indicate better alignment. Only included when method includes "boundary".

edge_f1

Numeric. Symmetric threshold-based boundary F1 (0-1). NA_real_ if either shared-domain boundary set is empty. Included when method includes "boundary".

edge_mhd

Numeric. Maximum of the two directed mean nearest-boundary distances, in map units; not classical maximum Hausdorff distance. NA_real_ if either shared-domain boundary set is empty. Included when method includes "boundary".

edge_chamfer

Numeric. Mean of the two directed mean nearest-boundary distances, in map units. NA_real_ if either shared-domain boundary set is empty. Included when method includes "boundary".

n_cells

Integer. Total number of valid cells analyzed.

n_edges_geo

Integer. Number of geomorphon boundary cells. Only included when method includes "boundary".

n_edges_cat

Integer. Number of categorical boundary cells. Only included when method includes "boundary".

contingency_table

Matrix. Cross-tabulation of geomorphon vs. categorical classes. Only included when method includes "nmi".

mean_null_nmi

Numeric. Arithmetic mean NMI across eligible deterministic spatial translations. NA_real_ if no shifts have paired-valid cells. Included only for methods "nmi" and "both".

delta_nmi

Numeric. Observed nmi minus mean_null_nmi; may be negative and is NA_real_ if either score is NA. Included only for methods "nmi" and "both".

nmi_null_shifts

Integer. Number of evaluated shifts eligible for the NMI null mean (shifts with paired-valid cells). Included only for methods "nmi" and "both".

mean_null_edge_f1

Numeric. Arithmetic mean edge F1 across shifts with nonempty edge sets. NA_real_ if no shifts are eligible. Included only for methods "boundary" and "both".

delta_edge_f1

Numeric. Observed edge_f1 minus mean_null_edge_f1; may be negative and is NA_real_ if either score is NA. Included only for methods "boundary" and "both".

edge_f1_null_shifts

Integer. Number of evaluated shifts eligible for the edge-F1 null mean (both edge sets nonempty). Included only for methods "boundary" and "both".

null_shifts_evaluated

Integer. Number of non-identity shifts evaluated for the null ensemble, shared by the requested metrics.

Note

Memory Requirements: This function performs edge detection on both input rasters. For small to medium rasters (< 1GB each), a fast C++ implementation is used. For larger rasters, the function automatically falls back to terra::boundaries() which is slower but more memory-efficient.

Since both rasters are processed simultaneously, the total memory requirement can approach 4x the size of a single raster in the worst case. For rasters larger than available RAM:

  • Process in tiles using terra::makeTiles()

  • Increase available system memory

  • Consider splitting the analysis into smaller regions

Information-Theoretic Concordance

Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) measures the mutual dependence between two categorical variables, independent of the specific class mappings. An NMI of 1 indicates perfect association, while 0 indicates independence. When NMI is requested, the result also includes directional homogeneity and completeness. With cat_rast as the reference, homogeneity = I(geo; cat) / H(cat) and completeness = I(geo; cat) / H(geo). Swapping the rasters swaps these two values but leaves NMI unchanged. When both entropies are positive, their harmonic mean equals NMI. A component with a zero entropy denominator is NA_real_; the other component is zero when defined. If both maps are constant, both components are NA_real_ while existing NMI remains 0. These additive components do not change the existing NMI calculation or values.

Boundary Alignment

Boundary alignment measures physical proximity between geomorphon and categorical boundaries. The edge_offset is the mean distance from each categorical boundary cell to the nearest geomorphon boundary cell, in map units of the input CRS. The edge_concordance is the proportion of categorical boundary cells within a threshold distance of the nearest geomorphon boundary cell. These legacy summaries retain their directional definitions and per-input valid masks.

The additive edge_f1, edge_mhd, and edge_chamfer summaries are symmetric. They detect boundaries for both maps only within their shared non-NA cells. edge_f1 is threshold-based: precision and recall are the proportions of boundary cells in each map within the threshold of a boundary in the other map, and F1 is their harmonic mean (range 0-1). It is not a kernel F1 or a one-to-one matched-boundary score. edge_mhd is the maximum of the two directed mean nearest-boundary distances; despite its name, it is not the classical maximum Hausdorff distance. edge_chamfer is the mean of those directed means. The distance summaries are non-negative and use input CRS map units. Each new score is NA_real_ if either shared-domain boundary set is empty.

Shared-domain edges use the existing eight-neighbor rule and exclude raster borders. Mask holes are not boundaries and do not block nearest-boundary distances. threshold_cells is multiplied by the x-resolution, including for rectangular cells; distance calculations use both cell dimensions. When input NA masks differ, legacy counts and directional summaries still use their existing per-input masks, so they need not describe the edges used by the new shared-domain scores.

For rasters to be comparable, they must have matching row and column counts, extents, and resolutions. Use terra::crop(), terra::resample(), or terra::disagg() to align rasters before calling this function.

The NMI is symmetric and normalized to the range 0-1, with higher values indicating stronger association regardless of how classes map to each other. Homogeneity and completeness are directional: cat_rast is the reference for their definitions, so swapping inputs exchanges the scores. If both marginal entropies are positive, their harmonic mean equals NMI. A zero denominator yields NA_real_ for that component; for two constant maps both components are NA_real_ and NMI remains 0. These fields are returned only by method = "nmi" or "both", not by "boundary". The boundary metrics are useful for validating whether geomorphological transitions correspond to ecological or pedological boundaries.

The additive spatial-null summaries compare the observed alignment with a deterministic sample of up to 128 non-identity circular translations of cat_rast; all candidate shifts are used when fewer than 128 exist. The schedule is defined for a raster with nr rows and nc columns by M = nr * nc - 1, S = min(128, M), and k_i = floor((i + 0.5) * M / S) for i = 0, ..., S - 1. For each index, q = k_i + 1 and the row/column shift is (dr, dc) = (q %/% nc, q %% nc). Using zero-based coordinates, the source category at destination (r, c) is [(r - dr) mod nr, (c - dc) mod nc]; the geomorphon map stays fixed. Outputs contain aggregate summaries only, not per-shift scores. The category values and their NA mask move together, and paired-valid cells are recomputed for each shift. NMI uses base-2 entropy and is zero when both marginal entropies are zero. Null edge F1 uses shared-valid eight-neighbor edges (excluding image borders) and toroidal Euclidean distances in cell coordinates with threshold_cells; a shift with either edge set empty is ineligible for its mean. Null summaries are arithmetic means over eligible shifts; deltas are observed minus mean and are not clamped. With no eligible shifts, the corresponding summary and delta are NA_real_ and its eligible count is zero. These are descriptive contrasts against this translation ensemble, not adjusted mutual information, calibrated scores, p-values, or evidence of statistical significance. NMI-null fields are returned only for method = "nmi" or "both"; edge-F1-null fields only for method = "boundary" or "both". null_shifts_evaluated is always returned. When spatial_null = FALSE, the ensemble is skipped, null means and deltas are NA_real_, and shift counts are 0L.

See also

geomorphons(), terra::boundaries()

Examples

library(terra)
library(rgeomorphon)

# Load example DEM
data("volcano", package = "datasets")
dem <- rast(volcano)
crs(dem) <- crs("EPSG:2193")
ext(dem) <- c(1756968, 1757578, 5917000, 5917870)

# Calculate geomorphons
geo <- geomorphons(dem, search = 7, simplify = TRUE)

# Create synthetic categorical map for demonstration
cat_map <- dem
values(cat_map) <- cut(values(dem), breaks = 5, labels = FALSE)

# Calculate concordance
conc <- geomorphon_concordance(geo, cat_map)
print(conc$nmi)
#> [1] 0.123542
print(conc$edge_concordance)
#> [1] 0.9707773
print(conc[c("edge_f1", "edge_mhd", "edge_chamfer")])
#> $edge_f1
#> [1] 0.7801114
#> 
#> $edge_mhd
#> [1] 26.19394
#> 
#> $edge_chamfer
#> [1] 14.6822
#>
